title: Understanding Intrinsic Socioeconomic Biases in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Using a fill-in-the-blank masked token task to measure the probability of LLMs associating various demographic groups with terms representing wealth versus poverty, quantified by a Poverty Association Ratio (PAR).
Comparing the Poverty Association Ratio (PAR) of male versus female demographic terms and names to evaluate differential associations with socioeconomic status.
Calculating the Poverty Association Ratio (PAR) for sentences containing different racial and ethnic terms, as well as race-associated names, to measure wealth and poverty stereotyping.
Assessing socioeconomic associations towards different religious groups by comparing their Poverty Association Ratios (PAR) in masked template sentences.
Evaluating how different marital status terms (e.g., married, divorced, widowed, single) correlate with wealth or poverty associations using the PAR metric.
Combining multiple demographic attributes (e.g., race, gender, marital status) and names in prompt templates to measure the compounded socioeconomic biases of intersecting identities.
